note: The two sets are essentially identical in content: same 19 claims, same values, quotes and bindings, with only a trivial ordering difference and Set A adding the condition 'load of laundry' to the clothes-drying eligibility claim (which is really the subject, not a condition). Both correctly capture the dishwasher temperature thresholds (120°F full, 115°F half), sensor redundancy, capacity, heated-drying disablement, and the Figure 8 weight-based scoring bands. Both also repeat the same facts under two names (scoring bands under 'Clothes Dryer Subcontest' and 'clothes-drying task', sensor count, 120°F, 115°F, wash/rinse cycle) and both omit several substantive rules on the page.
remarks: Both sets are near-duplicates of each other; the only delta is Set A's extra 'load of laundry' condition, which is immaterial. Both miss important page facts: the temperature-of-record rule (higher of two sensor readings, lower if the higher-reading sensor is defective), the definition of cycle 'interruption', cycle completion confirmed by audible/visible signal, permitted load states (empty/partial/full, soiled/clean), the two-loads-per-day requirement with separately scored double loads, the requirement that visible drying methods be demonstrated to the architecture and market appeal juries, and the Contest 9-1 lighting requirement. 'Dishwasher | operation mode | automatic' is a trivial fragment duplicating the minimum-cycle-requirements claim.
